title: The roadmap is a file, and the build reads it
thesis: A team's roadmap should be a file in the repo, checked by the build: plans survive where the work lives, and they stay true only when the build fails if they fall behind.

nodes.text: Plans evaporate because of where they live, not because teams stop caring: the plans kept next to the code outlived the ones kept on the wiki.

evidence.filled_by: last three retrospectives: checked-in plans survived, wiki plans died

nodes.text: Living in the repo keeps a plan alive but does not keep it true; without a check, entries go stale.

evidence.filled_by: eleven stale plan entries before the March 2024 script

nodes.text: Was the plan with eleven stale entries already a checked-in file before March 2024? The claim depends on it; the brief does not say.
What counted as a 'stale' entry, and who counted? The post should define it in one line.
Tie the plan to an event the build already sees: a version bump without a plan edit fails the build, and staleness disappears.

evidence.filled_by: script added March 2024: stale entries went from eleven to zero in a month

nodes.text: The usual objection is that a forced edit is a thoughtless edit; the answer is that a thoughtless edit is a visible diff someone can review, while a missing edit is invisible.

evidence.filled_by: the objection itself, as stated in the brief

nodes.text: Is there anything on the quality of the forced edits since March 2024 (reviewed, reverted, rubber-stamped)? Without it the rebuttal rests on reasoning alone, and the post should concede that much.
Close on the rule itself: the roadmap is a file in the repo, and a version that moves without the plan moving does not build.

evidence.filled_by: the March 2024 build check, restated as the rule
